newsitem.title: UK: Former Nadir aide to appeal conviction.
newsitem.headline: Former Nadir aide to appeal conviction.

text.p: Elizabeth Forsyth, former advisor to Polly Peck head Asil Nadir, said she would appeal her five-year conviction for handling stolen money later this week.
"Fortunately, the Court of Appeal has awarded me permission to appeal both against conviction and sentence," she said in a statement to Reuters, received on Monday.
The appeal will be heard from January 30.
A spokesman for the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said it would contest the appeal.
Forsyth, who denied the charges, was sentenced to five years in April last year after being found guilty of two counts of dishonestly handling 400,000 pounds.
She was chairman of South Audley Management, a firm set up by Nadir to deal with his family wealth before his Polly Peck fruit to electronics empire collapsed in 1990 under a mountain of debt.
Nadir himself faces charges connected to Polly Peck but fled to northern Cyprus in 1993.
